review_notes:
I read all 67 lines of the target file. It introduces no new definition, structure or type. It has three theorems (`map_branch_label_family`, `map_root_branch_family`, `iCondIndepFun_branch_product`) and one local instance, `MeasurableSingletonClass IsingSpin`, at line 49. The theorems state facts about Mathlib's own objects (`Measure.infinitePi`, `Measure.map`, `Measure.prod`, `IndepFun`, `iCondIndepFun`). They are proved by calling project lemmas (`infinitePi_map_disjoint_family`, `iCondIndepFun_latent_infinitePi`) and Mathlib lemmas (`IndepFun.map_prod_eq_prod_map_map`, `Measure.infinitePi_map_eval`). None of them builds a parallel version of a Mathlib concept, and the rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication.

The local instance is the only possible candidate, and I looked at it closely. `IsingSpin` is given `instance isingSpinMeasurable : MeasurableSpace IsingSpin := ⊤` in OAI/Probability/FreeIsing/Model.lean. Mathlib already has `instance : @DiscreteMeasurableSpace α ⊤` and `DiscreteMeasurableSpace.toMeasurableSingletonClass` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Defs.lean, lines 545–566). The same one-line local instance `⟨fun _ => trivial⟩` also appears in about 40 other project files. Even so, the instance is a proof of Mathlib's own class, not a competing concept, so it is really repeated proof boilerplate across the project. I also could not run Lean to check whether Mathlib's ⊤ instance already resolves this through `isingSpinMeasurable`, so I can't claim the local instance is redundant.

A tidier option would be one global `DiscreteMeasurableSpace IsingSpin` or `MeasurableSingletonClass IsingSpin` instance in Model.lean, but that is outside this rubric. Whether `IsingSpin` duplicates `Bool` or `SignType` would be a question about Model.lean, not this file, so I did not raise it.
